title: Valid Palindrome
description: A string counts as a palindrome if, after lowercasing every letter and discarding every character that isn't a letter or digit, it reads the same forwards and backwards. Given a string `s`, return `true` if it is a palindrome under this rule and `false` otherwise.

examples.input: s = "Was it a car or a cat I saw?"

constraints: s consists of printable ASCII characters
hints: Building a cleaned copy and comparing it to its reverse works. Can you check without allocating extra strings?
Place one pointer at each end and move them toward each other.
Skip pointers past non-alphanumeric characters, compare the two characters in lowercase, and return false on any mismatch.

solution.explanation: Use two pointers starting at both ends. Move the left pointer forward and the right pointer backward past any character that is not a letter or digit, then compare the lowercase versions of the two characters. If they differ the string is not a palindrome; if the pointers meet it is. Each character is visited once, giving O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
